narr: Northwest to southeast oriented bands of thunderstorms moved southeast, training over the same areas for several hours. A strong and very moist low-level wind flow fed the storms, with 850 mb winds generally from 35 to 40 knots. Tropical precipitable water values were estimated to be between 2 and 2.4 inches. Instability was sufficient for strong updrafts, with 1000 to 2000 J/kg of elevated cape near the confluence of the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers. The focus for the heaviest rain was from southeastern Missouri into far western Kentucky, northeast of a surface warm front draped across the central Missouri/Arkansas border.
ev: Water was over Highway 25 near the community of Arbor. The rainfall total from midnight to late afternoon at a site in west central Cape Girardeau County was 4.29 inches.

Several streets were flooded in Patton. Highway 34 was flooded in Marble Hill. Flash flooding of Crooked Creek inundated a park in Marble Hill. At the co-op station in Marble Hill, the 12-hour rainfall total ending late in the morning of the 3rd was 5.83 inches. The 36-hour rainfall total was 7.38 inches.

A photo posted on social media showed flooded streets and water threatening homes in Sikeston. Emergency management reported flash flooding of County Road 217 east of Chaffee. A trained spotter reported street flooding in Diehlstadt. A personal weather station in Benton measured 6.29 inches from midnight to late afternoon on the 3rd.
Streets were flooded, and there were homes with flooded basements in Advance. A personal weather station in Advance measured 5.86 inches from midnight to late afternoon on the 3rd.
